![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099242/assets/761e02a7613e2d1df4722b7bf6f0a7e1d0b5e7b6dec09d205a1e72a29b8c5eb8.png)

The shaded regions above represent the truth sets of the predicates $P(x,y)$ and $Q(x,y),$ defined over the universal set ${R}^{2}.$ Which of the following is the truth set of $P∨Q?$
worked_solution:
The truth set of $P∨Q$ represents the *union* of the truth sets of $P(x,y)$ and $Q(x,y):$

$$
{T}_{P∨Q}={T}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q}
$$

Therefore, to get the truth set of $P(x,y)∨Q(x,y),$ we take all the points that belong to ${T}_{P}$ or ${T}_{Q},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14099242/assets/9fc6aa4f7f220a14f33ed6269d598dd7aae24f6efac4caf80c8e7f5386450a5a.png)

**Note:** The points where the *solid* line meets the *dashed* curve belong to ${T}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q}$ since these points lie in ${T}_{P}.$
